title: Photographic Material Lab: Light & Lens Conservation
description: The user operates an antique photography studio where the barn lamp illuminates the antique camera as a subject. Users manipulate material properties (roughness, metalness, emissive intensity, anisotropy strength, clearcoat) across both objects while obeying a conservation law: total material energy budget is fixed at 10.0 units, so increasing one property on one object forces reductions elsewhere. Full undo/redo history tracks every adjustment.
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 with GLTFLoader and OrbitControls from CDN. Load AnisotropyBarnLamp.glb on the left and AntiqueCamera.glb on the right, both centered at ground level. Add a subtle ground plane with shadow-receiving MeshStandardMaterial. Use a directional light plus the barn lamp's emissive glow as key lighting. Camera starts at position (0, 1.5, 4) looking at origin.

IMPLEMENT A MATERIAL ENERGY CONSERVATION SYSTEM: Define a total energy budget of 10.0 units. Five material channels exist: roughness, metalness, emissiveIntensity, anisotropyStrength (lamp only), and clearcoat. Each channel has a value 0.0-2.0 per object. The sum of ALL channel values across BOTH objects must always equal exactly 10.0. When the user increases any slider, automatically proportionally decrease all other values to maintain the sum.

UI PANEL: Create an HTML overlay panel on the left with labeled sliders for each channel per object (10 sliders total). Display the current total budget with a colored bar (green when balanced, red during transition). Show each object's subtotal.

MULTI-INPUT COUPLING: Add a 'Link Mode' toggle. When enabled, adjusting roughness on the lamp simultaneously adjusts roughness on the camera inversely. Add a 'Transfer' button that moves 1.0 unit of energy from the selected channel of one object to the same channel of the other.

UNDO/REDO: Implement a history stack storing snapshots of all 10 values. Bind Ctrl+Z for undo and Ctrl+Shift+Z for redo. Show step count as 'History: X/Y' in the UI. Limit stack to 50 entries.

Apply material changes in real-time by traversing each model's scene graph and updating MeshPhysicalMaterial properties. Ensure anisotropy is only applied to lamp meshes. Add a 'Reset' button restoring default balanced state (1.0 each). Animate a subtle turntable rotation on the camera model. Render with tone mapping and antialiasing enabled.
